scope.product: unmodified original AnythingLLM with LM Studio on customer Mac Studio

measurementRules.uniquePositionNames: aggregation-sensitive breadth proxy; not ontology coverage
measurementRules.clauseCodePresence: audit-anchor proxy; not proof that all facts or roles in a clause were extracted
measurementRules.serverStreamFinished: transport completion only; finish reason and output token count were unavailable
measurementRules.contextMarker: highest visible context index; does not prove every chunk body arrived byte-complete
measurementRules.customerReady: requires factual, role, source, section, negative-state and completeness hard gates

settingsSemantics.workspaceVectorCount: namespace row count, not Top-N and not document completeness
settingsSemantics.maxContextSnippets: Top-N cap for retrieved contexts sent toward generation
settingsSemantics.similarityNoRestriction: threshold zero; does not expand Top-N
settingsSemantics.accuracyOptimized: separate native reranking path; does not identify the embedder and may have a smaller candidate pool
settingsSemantics.embeddingChunkCap: AnythingLLM characters, not LM Studio tokens
settingsSemantics.pinning: different full-context transfer path; not comparable to unpinned retrieval
settingsSemantics.modelIdentifier: part of AnythingLLM prompt-budget planning; wrong chat ID can cause compression even if LM Studio executes another loaded chat model
settingsSemantics.lmsPs: current loaded-model snapshot, not historical endpoint-use proof
settingsSemantics.promptCache: distinct from the vector database; audited quality runs had zero cached prompt tokens

dinghyIngestObservation.sepEosWarning: non-fatal in observed calls; retrieval-quality impact unquantified

notes: Pinned full-context path makes retrieval ranking and embedder quality non-isolatable.
No runtime log, finish reason or context-transfer proof.
Output ended cleanly and was far below available headroom; visible hard truncation is unlikely.
One very large CONTEXT 0 strongly indicates pinned full-document injection, not a normal Top-N6 retrieval test.
The answer cited a narrow page subset and turned missing retrieval into global not-found claims.
Top-N6 behavior is consistent with the output but not runtime-proven for this run.
Six retrieval contexts were injected.
Selected clauses were often detailed and cautious, but document breadth was low.
All ten N6 clause-code anchors were retained and sixteen were added.
Mandatory storm section was omitted and premium classifications remained largely unsupported.
No invented clause codes, but source, premium, role and mandatory-section hard gates failed.
The tree-or-mast clause was directionally inverted and major water and terror details were missing or wrong.
The retrieved package matched OAL-06 by context count and prompt-token count.
The answer was longer but duplicated and cross-assigned more content while losing audit anchors.
The output collapsed to a small pages-5-to-7 subset.
The same persisted configuration was repeated as OAL-08B, which proved the wrong chat-model contract and prompt compression.
AnythingLLM sent the chat request with model=dinghy while LM Studio fell through to Qwen.
The unknown chat-model contract triggered a 16384-token fallback and aggressive middle-out prompt compression.
Default-N32 removed a major context-delivery bottleneck and recovered many hard anchors.
All premium flags were unsupported no; source, section, role and cross-branch hard gates still failed.
Only the generator changed from OAL-09; the same retrieved context is strongly supported, not byte-proven.
Premium handling was more cautious, but glass facade, burglary and most water and storm facts disappeared.

controlledComparisons.result: N10 increased BGE breadth proxy from 26 to 36 unique positions and clause-code proxy from 10 to 26 without losing an N6 code anchor.
Dinghy breadth proxy changed only from 64 to 65 unique positions while clause-code proxy rose from 39 to 42; comparison is weaker because OAL-03 lacks runtime logging.
Dinghy was much broader; BGE was narrower but locally deeper. This evaluates the AnythingLLM pipeline, not pure embedder quality.
Dinghy reached 65 unique-position and 42 clause-code proxies versus BGE 36 and 26; BGE still contributed a small set of additional water-related anchors.
With the same ten contexts and 10699 prompt tokens, temperature zero produced a longer but more duplicated, less source-anchored and more cross-assigned answer.
Gemma was 33.9 percent faster end-to-end and more cautious on premium classification, but lost over half of Qwen's breadth proxy and many critical anchors.

campaignConclusions: No tested built-in one-prompt configuration passed the customer hard gates.
Pinned runs are extraction and attention tests, not valid embedder comparisons.
For the unpinned Accuracy path, Dinghy has the higher breadth proxies for this document and current pipeline, not a universal pure-embedder win.
Increasing Top-N materially helped BGE; Dinghy was near a breadth plateau between N6 and N10.
Default-N32 delivered much broader context, but free monolithic generation still broke roles, sources, mandatory sections and negative-state semantics.
Temperature zero and generator replacement did not repair the architecture.
The next experiment class is sectioned multi-pass extraction with deterministic source and completeness validation, not more free parameter roulette.
knownConfounders: Only one reference document was used; universality was not tested.
There was no complete fact-role oracle; row and clause-code counts are proxies.
Temperature 0.7 is stochastic and valid runs were generally not repeated.
Dinghy query text lacked the publisher-recommended task instruction.
Dinghy emitted a SEP/EOS GGUF metadata warning with unquantified retrieval impact.
Embedding chunk cap is measured in characters while LM Studio context is measured in tokens; oversize chunk truncation was not proven or excluded.
Qwen actually loaded 42496 context tokens despite AnythingLLM being configured for 65536; tested prompts fit, but output headroom and finish reason were unknown.
No chat-upload added-as-context path was tested.
